headline: Failed Senate bill would have blocked the EPA's stricter pollution standards for new cars and medium-duty vehicles starting with model year 2027.
what_it_does: This bill would have barred the Environmental Protection Agency from finalizing, carrying out, or enforcing its rule setting tougher emissions standards for new passenger cars, light trucks, and medium-duty vehicles. That rule sets stricter limits on greenhouse gases and other common air pollutants. The limits phase in from model year 2027 through 2032. The Senate voted the bill down on April 18, 2024.

who_it_affects.how: They would not have had to meet the EPA's stricter emissions limits for vehicles built for model years 2027 through 2032.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy new cars, SUVs, pickups, or vans
who_it_affects.how: The new vehicles they could buy starting with model year 2027 would not have been subject to the tougher pollution standards.
The agency would have been blocked from using funds to put in place or enforce this vehicle emissions rule.
